name: Photo Frame Editor – Custom Photo Frame Maker
author: dideron

sections.description:
Photo Frame Editor adds a frame editor to any page of your website. Visitors choose a photo, it is placed behind one of your transparent frames, they zoom, move, rotate and adjust it, then download (or share) a finished 1080×1080 image. It suits campaigns, events, schools, communities and brands that want people to create their own framed profile pictures.

Features

  • Add as many frames as you like (transparent PNG or WebP, square, 1080×1080 recommended).
  • Frame categories with filter buttons, and category cards.
  • Zoom, move, resize, rotate, flip, brightness and other adjustments, with mouse, touch or keyboard.
  • Mobile friendly layout with tabs and a fixed download bar.
  • Optional download counter per frame.
  • Bulk upload, ZIP export and ZIP import of frames.
  • Colors, text sizes, buttons and layout can be changed under Photo Frames → Appearance.

Privacy: photos are processed in the visitor’s browser and are never uploaded to your server.

Shortcodes

  • [pfd_editor] shows the editor. Options: limit="24", start="123" (frame ID to show first), track="1" (count downloads), share="1" (Share button on supported devices).
  • [pfd_editor category="birthday,wedding"] shows only those categories (operator="and" = frames in all of them, filter="1" shows category buttons above the frame slider; they are off by default).
  • [pfd_categories columns="3"] shows a card for every category. On the same page as the editor, clicking a card filters the editor in place. On any other page it links to the editor page (set under Appearance, or detected automatically).

Third-party library

This plugin bundles Fabric.js 7.4.0 (MIT license) in assets/js/fabric.min.js. Nothing is loaded from an external server.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the dideron-photo-frame-editor folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Photo Frames → Add New and upload a transparent frame image. Use the “Order” box to control the order (lower number first).
  4. Add the shortcode [pfd_editor] to any page.
sections.faq:
Are visitors’ photos stored on my server?

No. Photos are processed in the visitor’s browser only.

What data does the plugin store?

An anonymous download counter per frame, your Appearance settings, and a short-lived (about one minute) one-way hash of the visitor’s IP address used only to limit abuse of the counter.

Can I use more than one editor on a page?

No, one editor per page is supported. You can use [pfd_categories] on the same page.

Do frame categories have their own pages?

Yes. Each category with at least one published frame has an address like yoursite.com/frame-category/birthday/. It shows your editor page with that category already selected. You need pretty permalinks (Settings > Permalinks) and a page that contains [pfd_editor]. If a category address shows a 404, open Settings > Permalinks and click Save Changes once.

Do my frames get deleted when I delete the plugin?

Settings are removed. Your frames and their images are kept on purpose.

The visitor’s download looks wrong with a JPEG frame.

JPEG has no transparency, so the visitor’s photo is hidden behind it. Use a transparent PNG or WebP.
sections.changelog:
1.2.9

  • Category pages: each frame category has its own address (for example yoursite.com/frame-category/birthday/) that opens the editor page with that category selected. Works with page builders such as Elementor.
  • In the Photo Frames list, clicking a category name opens that category on the editor page. The Frame Categories screen shows each category’s page address and a View link.
  • The category buttons above the frame slider are off by default (use filter=”1″ to show them).
  • Category cards from [pfd_categories] all have the same height, with no underline or link colours from the theme.
  • The frame name is no longer shown under the preview on the editor page.

1.2.8

  • Fixed headings and text becoming too large on sites where a page builder (such as Elementor) sets global heading and paragraph styles.
  • Plugin name uses a plain hyphen so it shows correctly everywhere.

1.2.7

  • Plugin name changed to “Photo Frame Editor – Custom Photo Frame Maker”.
  • Removed the Quick View feature.

1.2.4

  • Appearance screen: quick-start buttons are aligned and the Editor page setting is always visible.

1.2.3

  • Appearance settings reorganised into Colors, Buttons and Layout tabs, with a live preview, quick-start color sets and a Reset button.
  • Hover colors are now made automatically (you can still choose them yourself).

1.1.7

  • Click the empty frame preview to choose a photo on desktop too, as on phones.

1.1.6

  • Slider arrows and the move/resize icon buttons are round on every theme.

1.1.5

  • Buttons and frame thumbnails keep their look when a theme styles all buttons and images.

1.1.4

  • The editor styles now load from a normal CSS file (assets/css/editor.css) in the page head, so caching and optimization plugins can find and handle them.

1.1.3

  • Fixed the editor briefly showing as unstyled HTML while the page loads.

1.1.2

  • Updated plugin name and assets.

1.1.1

  • Frame images now load even when the stored image address differs from the page address (http/https or www), with a clear error message if loading still fails.
  • Category cards use a single database query.

1.1.0

  • Renamed to Dideron Photo Frame Editor; new unique prefix (dpfr), shortcodes [pfd_editor] and [pfd_categories].
  • Fabric.js 7.4.0 is now bundled with the plugin; the CDN fallback and the one-click download were removed.
  • Styles and scripts are enqueued with the WordPress APIs instead of printed inline.
  • All admin text is translatable.
  • Removed the manual translation loader (WordPress.org loads translations automatically).

1.0.0

  • First release.
